description: One resonant mode of a struck object, built on the Max Mathews phasor filter: strike it with an impulse or a pulse and it rings at one frequency for a set time

params.text: Sets the frequency of the mode, three octaves either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Sets how long the mode takes to fall by 60dB, from silence to 7 seconds
Sets how loud the mode rings
Sets the phase the mode starts from, which changes the shape of the first few cycles rather than the pitch

inputs.text: The signal that excites the mode; an impulse or a short pulse is what makes it ring
Shifts the frequency of the mode, one volt per octave, multiplying whatever the knob is set to
Adds to the decay knob at a tenth of the knob's range per volt; the total is clamped at one and a half times the knob's own range, so the longest decay reachable is 10.5 seconds
Adds to the amplitude knob at a tenth of the knob's range per volt
Adds to the phase knob at a tenth of the knob's range per volt

outputs.text: The ringing mode, with everything below 30Hz filtered out

notes: it is a filter, not an oscillator: with nothing patched into the audio input it makes no sound at all.
several of these stacked on one excitation signal, each tuned to a different partial, is how a bell or a struck bottle is built.
